breathing_techniques.name: Box Breathing
breathing_techniques.description: Inhale for 4 counts, hold for 4, exhale for 4, hold for 4. Repeat 4–6 times.

breathing_techniques.name: 4-7-8 Breathing
breathing_techniques.description: Inhale for 4 counts, hold for 7, exhale slowly for 8 counts.
breathing_techniques.best_for: Sleep issues, anxiety, calming the nervous system

breathing_techniques.name: Belly Breathing
breathing_techniques.description: Place one hand on chest and one on belly. Breathe deeply so only your belly rises. Exhale slowly.

breathing_techniques.name: Alternate Nostril Breathing (Nadi Shodhana)
breathing_techniques.description: Close right nostril, inhale left. Close left, exhale right. Inhale right. Close right, exhale left. Repeat.

breathing_techniques.name: Pursed Lip Breathing
breathing_techniques.description: Inhale through nose for 2 counts, exhale through pursed lips for 4 counts.
breathing_techniques.best_for: Slowing breath, reducing shortness of breath

mindfulness_exercises.name: 5-4-3-2-1 Grounding
mindfulness_exercises.description: Name 5 things you see, 4 you can touch, 3 you hear, 2 you smell, 1 you taste. This brings you back to the present moment.

mindfulness_exercises.name: Body Scan Meditation
mindfulness_exercises.description: Lie down, close your eyes. Slowly bring attention from toes to head, noticing sensations without judgment.

mindfulness_exercises.name: Mindful Eating
mindfulness_exercises.description: Eat one meal slowly, savoring each bite. Notice flavors, textures, and aromas. Eat without distractions.

mindfulness_exercises.name: Loving-Kindness Meditation
mindfulness_exercises.description: Silently repeat: 'May I be happy. May I be healthy. May I be at peace.' Then extend these wishes to others.

mindfulness_exercises.name: Mindful Walking
mindfulness_exercises.description: Walk slowly, focusing on each step, your breath, and your surroundings. Leave your phone behind.

sleep_improvement_tips: Keep a consistent sleep schedule — wake up and go to bed at the same time daily
Avoid screens (phones, TV) 1 hour before bed
Keep your bedroom cool, dark, and quiet
Try a relaxing pre-sleep routine: warm bath, light reading, or gentle stretches
Avoid large meals within 2 hours of bedtime
Use the 4-7-8 breathing technique when lying down
Write down worries in a journal before bed to 'offload' them
Practice progressive muscle relaxation starting from your toes
mental_health_facts: 1 in 4 people worldwide will experience a mental health issue at some point in their lives.
Depression is one of the leading causes of disability globally, affecting over 280 million people.
Anxiety disorders are the most common mental health conditions, affecting around 4% of the global population.
Mental health conditions are treatable — 70–80% of people with depression respond positively to treatment.
Sleep and mental health are deeply connected; poor sleep worsens anxiety and depression.
Regular physical activity can reduce symptoms of anxiety and depression by up to 30%.
Social connection is one of the most powerful protectors of mental health.
Seeking help is a sign of strength, not weakness.
Mindfulness practices have been shown to reduce stress, anxiety, and depression.
Early intervention in mental health issues leads to significantly better outcomes.
